texts.preamble: Sunny George vs The Secretary on 4 June, 2020 Author: Alexander Thomas Bench: Alexander Thomas In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present The Honourable Mr. Justice Alexander Thomas Thursday, The 4Th Day Of June 2020 / 14Th Jyaishta, 1942 WP(C).No.10906 Of 2020(K) Petitioner: Sunny George Aged 50 Years S/O.George, Arakkal House, Valluvally West, Koonammavu.P.O, Ernakulam-683518 By Adv. Sri.K.R.Avinash (Kunnath)
texts.facts: The case set up in this Writ Petition (Civil) is as follows: The petitioner is the proprietor of a micro industrial unit in the name and style of "Super Traders" commenced operations in 2004. The business concern is engaged in the manufacturing and sales of packaged food products like Chili powder, Turmeric Powder, coriander powder etc. The products are being marketed in the brand name "Tasma". Industrial unit has been issued with license under Section 232 & 233 of the Kerala Panchayath Raj Act 1994 in the year 2004 itself and such license was being periodically renewed ever since. When petitioner has applied for renewal of license for the present financial year, on 12.03.2020 the Secretary of Panchayath has issued latter dated 05.05.2020 to the petitioner stating that the 4 th respondent has filed a complaint against the industrial unit that it may cause health issues to him and family members and so the petitioner was required to produce Consent to operate from the District Medical Officer & Pollution Control Board (PCB). Ever since ..3.. commencement industry was having pollution control measures. It was upgraded on knowing about the compliant and petitioner has submitted application for Consent to operate to the Pollution Control Board on 14.05.2020 and paid the fees along with compounding fee for not obtaining consent for previous years. The PCB authorities have conducted an inspection on 15.05.2020 in the industrial unit stated to be based on a complaint dated 08.05.2020 made by the 4th respondent and the Environmental Engineer has issued Exhibit P8 stop memo dated 21.05.2020 to the petitioner directing that the industrial unit should function only after obtaining the consent to operate from the Pollution Control Board. But the 3rd respondent Environment Engineer is not considering and taking any steps on Exhibit P6 application submitted by the petitioner on 14.05.2020 for issuance of Consent to operate. The industrial unit is installed with upgraded equipment and installations for controlling pollution as per the relevant norms and rules, and thus perfectly entitled to be issued with consent to operate from the PCB and hence the delay on the part of the Pollution Control Board in considering the application of the petitioner for consent to operate will detrimentally affect the ..4.. lawful trade being carried on by the petitioner which is his livelihood. It is in the light of the abovesaid facts and circumstances that the petitioner has filed the instant Writ Petition (Civil) with the following prayers: " Sunny George vs The Secretary on 4 June, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133670970/ 2 i. declare that Exhibit P8 stop memo issued by the 3rd respondent is illegal. ii. declare that the 3rd respondent Environmental Engineer is bound to consider and pass orders on Exhibit P6 application for Consent to operate submitted by the petitioner. iii. issue a writ of Certiorari or such other writ or order and thereby [LEAKAGE_MASK] Exhibit P8 stop memo issued by the 3rd respondent Environmental Engineer. iv. issue a writ of mandamus or such other writ or order directing the 3rd respondent to consider and pass orders on Exhibit Po application submitted by the petitioner. 3. The complaint of the petitioner is directed mainly against the delay in consideration of Ext.P-6 application dated ..5.. 14.5.2020 submitted by the petitioner to the 3rd respondent Environmental Engineer of the Kerala State Pollution Control Board for grant of consent to operate his industrial unit, and that any further delay would highly detrimentally affect the petitioner's interest, as the petitioner has been disabled from functioning of unit in view of Ext.P-8 stop memo dated 21.5.2020 issued by the 3rd respondent, etc. 4.
texts.arguments: The counsel for the petitioner would also submit that, now the petitioner has recently received a communication from the 3rd respondent instructing him to upgrade some of the facilities in his unit, and that the petitioner would require atleast 10 days time to comply with such remedial measures and upgradation, etc. 5. Sri . T.Naveen, learned Standing Counsel for the Kerala State Pollution Control Board appearing for R-3 would submit that, even going by the petitioner's pleadings Ext.P-6 application has been submitted only on 15.5.2020, and that in view of the problems arising out of the COVID-19 pandemic, reasonable time will be required for taking final decision on the matter in Ext.P-6 application, etc.
texts.petitioner_arguments: The counsel for the petitioner would also submit that, now the petitioner has recently received a communication from the 3rd respondent instructing him to upgrade some of the facilities in his unit, and that the petitioner would require atleast 10 days time to comply with such remedial measures and upgradation, etc. 5.
texts.respondent_arguments: Sri . T.Naveen, learned Standing Counsel for the Kerala State Pollution Control Board appearing for R-3 would submit that, even going by the petitioner's pleadings Ext.P-6 application has been submitted only on 15.5.2020, and that in view of the problems arising out of the COVID-19 pandemic, reasonable time will be required for taking final decision on the matter in Ext.P-6 application, etc.
